notes: Data came from the Next.js App Router RSC flight payload embedded in the leaderboard document (self.__next_f), not from a separate XHR/fetch endpoint, same as the 20260902 scrape. The DOM script tags containing `self.__next_f.push(...)` were read directly from document.querySelectorAll('script') and eval'd with a stubbed push() to capture the (id, stringChunk) pairs, since window.__next_f itself is emptied by the Next.js runtime after hydration on this page.

The combined flight text contains TWO top-level "models":[ arrays: the first (offset ~10.6k chars) is a lightweight model-picker list (slug/name/effort/release/creator only, 636 entries) used by a dropdown component; the second (offset ~289.7k chars) is the full leaderboard payload with every benchmark/metric field (636 entries). Only the second was used for raw.json/normalized.json. This two-array structure was not called out in the 20260902 meta.json and should be checked for on future scrapes of this page.

raw.json is the verbatim `models` array (second occurrence) from that payload (636 model entries, ~3.35 MB), unmodified except that it was extracted via balanced-bracket text slicing (not a regex) and JSON.parse'd in-browser via evaluate_script with filePath, then saved directly to disk.

The RSC payload uses the literal string "$undefined" as a serialization sentinel for fields the server didn't send (as documented in the 20260902 notes for per-benchmark cost fields). This scrape treats "$undefined" as absent everywhere, the same as null, before building normalized.json - e.g. Muse Spark 1.3 (max) has $undefined for all output-speed/latency metrics and those rows are correctly omitted.
Benchmark display names are a mapping of the payload field keys to their commonly used names, identical to the 20260902 mapping; every record keeps the exact original key in `source_field`.

MMLU-Pro, AIME and LiveCodeBench are still NOT present in this payload. A new field `cweBench` appeared in the schema (present as a key on all 636 records) but its value is "$undefined" for every single model, so it carries no data yet and was left out of benchmarks_captured, matching the no-invented-values policy.
`rank` is present only on Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index records and is derived by sorting all 623 models that report a non-undefined index descending; it is not a rank published by the site.
`cost_usd` on every record is the model-level blended price per 1M tokens at a 3:1 input:output ratio (field price1mBlended0To3To1), attached as cost context; it is not a per-benchmark cost.
`date` is the model release date (releaseDate) reported by the site, not the scrape date.
Score scales are as published: eval scores are fractions 0-1 (e.g. gpqa), index values are on their own scales. No rescaling applied.
Null and "$undefined" values were omitted rather than filled.
changes_vs_20260902: model_count 634 -> 636 (net +2 model/effort entries in the leaderboard payload); row_count 17200 -> 17254.
Models with a reported (non-$undefined) Intelligence Index: 621 -> 623.

New model families visible in this scrape that were checked per the task: Muse Spark 1.3 (present, multiple effort variants: max, xhigh) and Gemini 3.8 Flash (present, effort variants: low, medium, high).

Discovered that the leaderboard RSC payload contains two separate "models":[ arrays (a slim picker list and the full data array); the 20260902 scrape script presumably located the correct one via the same content, but this was made explicit and verified by content (checked for intelligenceIndex/gpqa proximity) rather than assumed from the first match this time.
New raw field `cweBench` appeared in the per-model schema but is $undefined for all 636 models, so no new benchmark data was actually added; not included in benchmarks_captured.
No fields disappeared from the 20260902 metrics/benchmarks schema.
No page failures; single navigation to the leaderboard URL succeeded, all 53 self.__next_f.push script tags evaluated without error.
